etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English durable, from Old French durable, from Latin dūrābilis (“lasting, permanent”), from dūrō (“harden, make hard”).

definitions.definition: Able to resist wear or decay; lasting; enduring.
(economics) A durable thing, one useful over more than one period, especially a year.

quote.citation: 1989, Robert A. Pollak, The theory of the cost-of-living index, page 188:
quote.text: In a frictionless world with perfect rental markets, there is an unambiguous cost associated with the use of a durable for a single period.
